Hey Guys, i thought about posting a newly thread in this section, however decided to just make a new post in this original thread.

Im kind of starting to collect pictures of "No-Brainer PO setups" that can be taken without waiting for PA confirmation, because the fact to get in the trade just is prior to waiting for correct PA.

So this will help me to look for very clear Price Action in the past that is still fresh and waits to be tested, especially (!) on the higher timeframes.

Here are a few examples I already have (zone of interest in orange):

Note that these setups already ocurred, these are just examples for myself to draw the orange box and set the PO at the upper line of the orange rectangle and this is how price should react and these zones MOST of the time if we draw the zones correctly.

USDCHF - facts before the trade: + Strong engulfing pattern (even on LTF) + first real retest of broken + three tap (down channel)

GBPCHF - facts before the trade: + clear rally results in a very clear H4 base with a even better break of this level + compression into the level

GBPUSD - facts before the trade: + a clear base on H1 that got broken + left the base with strong bear bars and even gapped + took out the latest rally downleg of the base arrival with no problem, indicating price was too cheap

GBPUSD - facts before the trade: + a clear resistance area on HTF that got tested several times + SFP: This is very important. Price gapped above the resistance area but closed within the resistance area with a long hammer down on daily. Lots of lots of accumulation of retail buy orders here for the sellers to go short. This is the best scenario at strong areas to cause major reversals. If you search for this "failed-to-break" and "stay-in-the-zone" pattern with a clear bar on the HTF, you will find awesome trading opportunities.

GBPJPY - facts before the trade: + it was a very bullish uptrend during the time this trade happened, so looking for LONG POs + price kind of made a small resistance and broke this level big style with a move just over 300 pips + we even had a clear smaller TF base that got broken by an engulfing bar, so this is the area of interest for the PO. (upper orange zone)

If its okay for the admins, we could transfer this in a new thread, if not, I would love comments and posts from all RTM members to collect more of this

decisions. The realization already is that price is only ever moving from one decision point to another, and the invariant at any decision point (DP) is value. If price falls away from an area, its decided price is too expensive - this is the invariant at this level at this moment. The basis to that invariant is the amount of supply that such a DP attracts. After the decision is made, different market participants may then join in, not until, adding more supply and helping the invariant hold when price returns - RTM style trading does exactly that.

v=ov9kH54Z-

dM

The core move that we see is a move up into a space we can reason about, which is, if upwards, an DP area where it was previously decided price was too expensive. There will probably be resting limit orders, as well as active traders watching as price returns to the area. Everyone is waiting for some confluence depending on their trading modality, but at some point the supply/demand invariant holds or it breaks. So the move up happens, and the sign that price is too expensive is the engulf down. Some engulfs matter more than others it seems, and if a key DP is engulfed, price ascends in the winds of demand that it consumed, until those winds fade out and price returns to that last place where supply was overwhelming. This is the FTB trade down. And of course, the key to the DP is how the decision was made - was it timid, or was there conviction.

But the primary takeaway is that price is bouncing between decisions on value. One cannot say that its just some invariant that holds until price at a certain level in the book hits zero, because it is dropping as well as rising as the dynamics of the decisions about value play out.

I probably completely botched this but here's my try at it. A lot of the turns in the weekly chart could be explained by weekly structures, but some of them needed LTF to explain it. Earlier was easiest to decipher, later on I ran into some areas I couldn't quite understand.

The big weekly picture, with explanations and inserts as I saw necessary:

1) Price hits the upper boundaries of a compression area and bounces. Price then decides to break into compression and makes it through the S/R flip.

2) Price starts to encounter demand below and bounces between demand and the S/R flip. Price then decides to break demand, with the important decision area outlined below.

3) The low here I don't really understand. To the left, there's an area of used demand but the move out of it wasn't very impressive to begin with so maybe this is one of those news driven turns?

4) Price rallies up to the decision point outlined in #2's chart and bounces, consuming the remaining orders. Price then creates new weekly demand before continuing higher.

5) Price bounces from our decision point to engulf the compression and forms weekly supply right below.

6) Bounce from demand.

7) Temporary rejection of price from supply. Price then moves up through supply. I didn't notice any specific decision points as to where it necessarily said "this supply is over with!", so maybe someone could help me out on this one.

8 & 9) Supply becomes demand, price re-tests our ignored supply and moves higher to fresh supply at 9.

Big consolidation area better explained on the daily charts with several caps on price forming. Eventually price breaks down and forms demand, rallying to form the FTR (?) in 10.

10) Somewhere in the wick to the left is our decision point to break the daily demand and go lower; upon returning here, price drops. A nice supply level is left here after failing to re-enter our previous price action zone.

11) Price ignores demand and makes a decision to go lower.

12) Price bounces from supply which wasn't consumed by the bounce at 6.

13) Price re-visits the decision point at 11 and drops.

14) Bounce from second-touch demand originating from March 8th.

15) Low of the swing turns before breaking the low of the last swing but the exact spot it moves from doesn't seem to have any significance.

16) Not sure about this one either. Price seems to be in the middle of a move where it turns exactly.

17) Price bounces from the base of our flag and forms demand.

18) Not really any specific PA to the left that would suggest a bounce here.

19 & 21) Bounces off of demand formed at 17.

20) Price bounces from the decision to go lower found on the H4 charts.
